static_traits.name: Liu Chen
static_traits.social_status: Relationships with family and friends strained by job-seeking views, but has one supportive friend to confide in
static_traits.medical_history: no history of similar psychological problems; no past psychotherapy;No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, highly cooperative, anxious emotions; thinking shows tendencies of catastrophizing, overgeneralization, jumping to conclusions (predicting the future) and mental filtering

basic_info.main_problem: I believe I can never find a daytime job because I prefer nights over days. This belief makes me feel hopeless and unmotivated, and makes me avoid applying for daytime positions, only seeking night-shift work.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because I noticed this belief limits my job opportunities and affects my overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Turned down a professional basketball opportunity a few months ago; since then gradually formed the belief that 'I cannot handle daytime work', accompanied by hopelessness and insufficient motivation; job-seeking pressure is seen as a factor worsening this belief.
Long-term preference for a nighttime schedule, but never truly tried full-time daytime work; this preference gradually became equated with 'being unable to adapt to daytime work'.

core_beliefs: I am not suited for daytime work
I lack the ability to adapt to a daytime schedule

special_situations.event: When needing to search or browse daytime job postings
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I take daytime work, I will stay exhausted, not adapt, and perform very poorly
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids applying for daytime positions; only focuses on and applies to night-shift positions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I definitely cannot hold on; it will be miserable

special_situations.event: Imagines the daily arrangements and performance once accepting a daytime job
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot fully adapt to a daytime schedule, it equals failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining a nighttime schedule, not trying daytime positions to avoid 'failure'
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not adapt well enough, I will be utterly worthless

special_situations.event: Talking with family or friends about job seeking and routines
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I try daytime work but perform poorly, they will look down on me or negate me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces discussing this topic with them, insists on only looking for night shifts to avoid being judged
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think I am no good/are harshly judging me

special_situations.event: Recalling having declined a professional basketball opportunity
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Missing that opportunity means I will easily fail in the future too
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using 'night preference' as the reason for not trying daytime work, to avoid failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I missed the only opportunity; nothing I do afterwards will go smoothly

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be understood and live by one's own rhythm, making choices free from external pressure
core_conflict.fear: Fearing that change will bring failure and long-term exhaustion, and being judged or negated by others for it
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of control and lowering anxiety by avoiding daytime positions
Justifying not trying with the 'night preference' rationale, thereby avoiding the sense of failure

object_relations.self_representation: A misunderstood job seeker who may be incompetent
object_relations.object_representation: Others (family/friends/society) who do not understand and exert pressure

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When demanded or encouraged to apply for daytime positions, or asked why not try daytime work
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tending to believe others are judging oneself; once an attempt fails one will be negated
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly emphasizing the rationale of 'more suited to nights/not suited to days' in a calm but firm tone, avoiding concrete commitments, instead stressing the advantages and fit of night shifts.

manifestations: Feeling hopeless and unmotivated due to believing 'I cannot handle daytime work'
Job choices are markedly narrowed, only seeking night shifts, daily productivity declines
Doubting future direction and sense of worth after turning down the professional basketball opportunity
outcomes: Avoids applying for day jobs, only searches for night-shift opportunities
Disrupted sleep rhythm and decreased life efficiency
Relationship tension with family and friends, worsened experience of being misunderstood

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Using absolutist expressions like 'I can never handle daytime work'
Overly limiting job options and only looking at night shifts due to worrying about poor adaptation
Tending to wait and see when exploring daytime positions, not committing to avoid directly facing challenges

positive_force: Motivated to seek help and proactively seeking counseling
Possessing some self-reflection ability, having tried challenging ingrained beliefs on one's own
Having one supportive friend to confide in and be encouraged by
negative_force: Significant cognitive biases such as catastrophizing, overgeneralization, jumping to conclusions (predicting the future) and mental filtering
Avoids applying for daytime positions, only seeks night shifts, leading to limited job opportunities
Hopelessness and insufficient motivation lower the likelihood of action
Relationship tension with family and friends, subjectively feeling misunderstood
Day-night rhythm is disordered and productivity drops, intensifying the negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Avoids applying for day jobs, only searches for night-shift positions
antecedent: Browsing daytime positions on job platforms
Being advised by others to try daytime work
Thinking about situations requiring adaptation to a daytime schedule
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophic predictions based on 'it will be miserable/cannot adapt' and the belief of 'I am not suited'; negative self-attribution after turning down the professional basketball opportunity reinforced this belief
target_behavior.function: Escaping anticipated failure, exhaustion and being judged, gaining short-term safety and anxiety relief
target_behavior.consequence: Limited job-seeking opportunities, unstable employment or continued unemployment; disrupted sleep schedule, decreased life efficiency; relationship tension with family and friends and reinforced hopelessness

target_behavior.behavior: Strong anxiety and hopelessness when searching for or imagining daytime work
antecedent: Actively searching or being asked to search for daytime jobs
Imagining oneself in daytime work scenarios and performance
target_behavior.core_reason: Equating emotional experience with facts (emotional reasoning), certain predictions of a negative future and overgeneralization
target_behavior.function: Rapidly lowering anxiety by stopping the search or turning to night shifts (escaping discomfort)
target_behavior.consequence: A negative reinforcement cycle reinforcing avoidant behavior, further lowering the likelihood of trying daytime positions
